frame_metadata.gps_note: Every frame carries capture time with a -04:00 offset and the F0 build's 9-key GPS block. But from the first label (f0004, 16:18) to the exterior (f0028, 16:33) every frame carries the same fix, taken at 16:16:20 by the entrance: the phone produced no new fix indoors. The fix places the take at Cooper Hewitt; it says nothing about where in the building a frame was shot.

verification_note: Accessioned 2018, after the museum's published dataset was last updated (2018-01-10), and not in the Smithsonian Open Access API (CC0 records only). The catalog site answers scripts with a request-verification page. Transcribed from the label frame and checked against the work photo; per §4.7 this is a label claim, not a catalog fact. Upgrade to a catalog check when a source that holds the record is reachable. The panel's other two objects are in the dataset and verified there.

shared_panel.note: One tall panel, three tombstones stacked, each beside a black silhouette of its object — a kettle-shaped vessel, a ring telephone, a tall vase. The silhouette is the only thing tying a tombstone to an object in the case; there are no numbers or positions. The work photo shows the telephone, with a marbled ceramic vase from a neighbouring case at the bottom edge.

traps.date_shaped_accession: The number reads as a date, and the tester answered 'no number' on the spot. Cooper Hewitt's key is acquisition year, lot, item. See data/venues/cooper-hewitt.json traps. Here the locator ranked the right object first, and all three panel numbers were offered.
traps.loan_flag_wrong: Tagged 'loan, no accession' on the spot. All three objects are Cooper Hewitt's own.
traps.life_dates_as_ranges: '1834–1904', '1848–1933' and the title date '1879–82' are all two groups joined by a dash; the locator's YEAR_RANGE skips them, correctly.
